pairs: Will you yourselves not also be plundered?
And woe to you who despise!
Will you yourselves not also be despised?
When you will have completed your plundering,
you will have ceased acting with contempt,
you will be treated with contempt.
For we have waited for you.
Be our arm in the morning
et salus nostra in tempore tribulationis.
and our salvation in the time of tribulation.
From the voice of the Angel, the people fled.
et ab exaltatione tua dispersæ sunt gentes.
And from your exultation, the nations were scattered.
Et congregabuntur spolia vestra sicut colligitur bruchus,
And your spoils will be gathered together,
velut cum fossæ plenæ fuerint de eo.
just as the locusts are collected when the ditches have become filled with them.
because he has lived on high.
He has filled Zion with judgment and justice.
Et erit fides in temporibus tuis:
And there will be faith in your times:
timor Domini ipse est thesaurus ejus.
For the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
Behold, outside, those who see will cry out.
The Angels of peace will weep bitterly.
Travelers have ceased along the paths.
The earth has mourned and languished.
Lebanon has been confounded and desecrated.
et factus est Saron sicut desertum,
And Sharon has become like a desert.
et concussa est Basan, et Carmelus.
And Bashan and Carmel have been struck together.
Now I will lift myself up!”
You will give birth to stubble.
spiritus vester ut ignis vorabit vos.
Your own spirit will devour you like fire.
Et erunt populi quasi de incendio cinis;
And the people will be like the ashes from a fire.
They will be consumed by fire like a bundle of thorns.
listen to what I have done!
The sinners in Zion are terrified;
trembling has taken hold of the hypocrites.
Quis poterit habitare de vobis cum igne devorante?
Who among you is able to live with a devouring fire?
quis habitabit ex vobis cum ardoribus sempiternis?
Who among you will live with an everlasting flame?
Qui ambulat in justitiis et loquitur veritatem,
The one who walks in justice and speaks the truth,
qui projicit avaritiam ex calumnia, et excutit manus suas ab omni munere,
who casts out avarice with oppression and shakes all bribes from his hands,
qui obturat aures suas ne audiat sanguinem,
who blocks his ears so that he may not listen to blood,
et claudit oculos suos ne videat malum.
and closes his eyes so that he may not see evil.
Such a one will live on high;
the fortification of rocks will be his lofty place.
Bread has been given to him;
Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus,
His eyes will see the king in his elegance;
they will discern the land from far away.
Your heart will meditate on fear.
Where are those who ponder the words of the law?
Where are the teachers of little ones?
You will not look upon a shameless people,
ita ut non possis intelligere disertitudinem linguæ ejus, in quo nulla est sapientia.
For you are not able to understand the dissertation of a tongue in which there is no wisdom.
a tabernacle that can never be taken away.
nec auferentur clavi ejus in sempiternum,
Its stakes will not be taken away forever,
et omnes funiculi ejus non rumpentur:
nor will any of its cords be broken.
quia solummodo ibi magnificus est Dominus noster:
For only in that place has our Lord been magnified.
It is a place of rivers,
non transibit per eum navis remigum,
No ship with oars will cross through it,
nor will the great Greek ship pass through it.
For the Lord is our judge.
sic erit malus tuus ut dilatare signum non queas.
Your mast will be such that you will not be able to unfurl a flag.
Then the spoils of much plunder will be divided.
The lame will seize the spoils.
He who is nearby will not say:
populus qui habitat in ea, auferetur ab eo iniquitas.
The people who live in it will have their iniquity taken away from them.
